tex_content.html:
Lemma
[velocity-seeded parallel orthonormal frame]

↗ def:dc-ch5-2-1

Let $\gamma :[a,b]\to M$ be a geodesic whose initial velocity is a unit vector. Then there is a parallel orthonormal frame $e_1(t),\dots ,e_n(t)$ along $\gamma $ (parallel: $De_i/dt=0$; orthonormal: $\langle e_i(t),e_j(t)\rangle =\delta _{ij}$ for all $t$) whose distinguished member is the velocity, $e_{n_0}(t)=\gamma '(t)$ for all $t\in [a,b]$.
Proof

\sketch Extend $\gamma '(a)$ to an orthonormal basis and parallel-transport that basis. Parallel transport preserves the metric, while uniqueness identifies the transported copy of $\gamma '(a)$ with the parallel field $\gamma '$.

□
